source:
Vera: We should switch to the four-day week; our output per hour is already the highest in the sector.
Hugo: Output per hour is high because we cut training, not because of any schedule magic.
Vera: Even if the training cuts explain all of it, I would still switch because burnout is unsustainable.

extraction.mainQuestion: Should the company switch to a four-day week?

positions.label: Switch to four days
positions.thesis: The company should switch to a four-day week; productivity supports it and burnout demands it.
positions.steelman: Sector-leading output shows headroom, and unsustainable burnout is a reason independent of the productivity number.

groundingQuotes.quote: We should switch to the four-day week

positions.label: Keep five days
positions.thesis: The output number reflects training cuts, so it is no reason to change the schedule.
positions.steelman: If the productivity signal is an artifact of reduced training, the schedule case collapses.

groundingQuotes.quote: Output per hour is high because we cut training, not because of any schedule magic.

claims.statement: Output per hour is the highest in the sector.

groundingQuotes.quote: our output per hour is already the highest in the sector

claims.statement: Output per hour is high because training was cut.

disagreementCandidates.question: Why is output per hour so high?
disagreementCandidates.summary: Vera reads it as schedule headroom; Hugo attributes it to training cuts.
disagreementCandidates.resolutionCondition: Output data controlling for training changes.

disagreementCandidates.question: Is current burnout unsustainable?
disagreementCandidates.summary: Vera treats burnout as a standalone reason to switch.
disagreementCandidates.resolutionCondition: Agree on a burnout threshold that would trigger a schedule change.

claimStakeCandidates.targetConclusion: The company should switch to a four-day week.
claimStakeCandidates.consequence: Vera says she would still switch even if the training cuts explained the entire output number.

groundingQuotes.quote: Even if the training cuts explain all of it, I would still switch because burnout is unsustainable.

caveats: The output ranking and burnout level are asserted, not measured.
